name: process-design
description: Process Design with extra benefits — a thought-partner skill that walks you from a fuzzy intuition to a build-ready spec via Working Backwards, metrics-first design, Elon's algorithm, gap probing, TDD-style verification, drafting, adversarial verification, and an implementation-agnostic build handoff. Bundles qa-agents (adversarial three-agent review, now with a root-cause-analysis pass on confirmed major findings) for Phase 7 verification, the dmaic skill family (Define / Measure / Analyze / Improve / Control) for metrics review cycles, elons-operating-algorithm (one-shot pressure test that runs Elon's full 5-step algorithm against any artifact — spec, plan, architecture, roadmap — and produces a structured deletion-first review), test-loop (builds the executable regression suite that locks a spec's decision rules and conventions into tests and surfaces real bugs in the process — the executable companion to dmaic-control), build-workflow (compiles a verified spec into a runnable Claude Code Workflow script and tests every gate's fail branch live before marking the spec implemented), system-map (the system-altitude view for many interacting processes: process inventory, artifact contracts, derived wiring diagram, four stopping tests that bound decomposition depth, deletion sweep, and a top-down/bottom-up reconciliation loop), and system-build-loop (the autonomous ramble-in, ratified-system-out orchestrator: charter, map, three-layer research fan-out, soft-fail design descent, selective builds, reconcile ascent, and one batched decision review — asks nothing mid-run except at two defined stuck points). All thirteen skills callable independently.
